newsitem.title: FRANCE: French TV channels cut screen violence - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: French TV channels cut screen violence - watchdog.

text.p: French television channels have been showing less violence in programmes likely to be seen by children, thanks to a voluntary code put in place last year, France's broadcasting watchdog said on Wednesday.
A decline in ethical and advertising standards in recent years has been halted due to regular dialogue with the TV channels, the Conseil Superieur de l' Audiovisuel (CSA) said in a statement.

"The Conseil was able to observe a beginning of improvement in programming by private channels of the representation of violence on the screen, notably in the last quarter of 1996," the CSA said in its 1996 review of France's three private terrestrial television stations.

It said conventions it signed last year with the three channels included a voluntary code to protect children and teenagers by classifying programmes, by their timing and by carrying a symbol on the screen corresponding to the suitability of films for particular age groups.

"During 1996 the Conseil, thanks to a permanent dialogue with the management of the channels, warned of and ended the drift seen in previous years in the ethics of programmes and advertising standards," the CSA said.
However, there had been a few breaches which prompted the CSA to intervene, it said, giving no details.
The CSA also said the three channels, TF1 , M6 and Canal Plus , had more than fulfilled their obligations to carry a fixed percentage of programmes of French and European origin last year.
TF1 and Canal Plus had both more than halved the time they broadcast American fiction programmes, while M6 had increased the time it broadcast European fiction by 18.8 percent.

"The place now occupied by European and French fiction at peak watching times on the private channels shows their real and efficient contribution to the development of a national broadcasting heritage," the CSA said.

The three channels together spent 1.61 billion francs ($271.2 million) in 1996 on co-production of French and European series, of which TF1 put up 1.05 billion francs, M6 321 million francs and Canal Plus 237 million francs.
TF1 and M6 spent 248 million francs on co-producing films, of which 197 million came from TF1.
Canal Plus spent 1.07 billion francs on acquiring European film rights last year, of which 795 million was spent on French language films. ($ = 5.936 French Francs)
